content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes in historical data (e.g., 65+ → forecast jumps to 60+ but then fails to catch the rebound).
- Tends to overreact to recent low prices, producing overly pessimistic forecasts when prices are falling.
- Underestimates late-period (last 5–10 days) price increases, especially when true outcomes show strong upward momentum.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing price rebounds after troughs — forecasts lag behind true price recovery by 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model often forecasts prices to return to historical averages too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Overshoots in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 10–20) when true prices are rising, then undercorrects later.
- When historical prices are volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes, leading to underprediction of volatility-driven spikes.
